# EasyAnalysis

> EasyAnalysis is a free, browser-based platform for running statistical, machine-learning
> and spatial/geospatial analysis by pointing and clicking — no coding required. It runs
> entirely in the user's web browser (R compiled to WebAssembly), so uploaded data never
> leaves the user's computer. Live at https://easyanalysis.vercel.app

## What it is

EasyAnalysis lets students, researchers and professionals run rigorous analyses on their own
data without writing code. Upload a dataset, pick what you want to do, click Run, and read the
results in plain English — including model metrics and an interpretation. An AI Co-Pilot can
run analyses for you and explain plots and results, grounded strictly in the tool's own methods
(no external hallucination).

The tool is domain-general (works for any tabular or spatial data). Its founding reference
domain is Finnish National Forest Inventory (NFI/VMI) data for forest trafficability and
tree-growth modelling, but nothing in the core is forestry-specific.

## Key features

- **Point-and-click analysis** — no scripting. Nothing computes until you press Run.
- **Runs 100% locally in the browser** via WebAssembly (webR). No data is uploaded to any
  server; closing the tab clears the session. Strong privacy by design.
- **AI Co-Pilot** — ask it to run an analysis, or to explain a plot or a result. It is
  grounded in the app's own data and methods and will not invent numbers or column names.
- **Recommend** — a plain-English read on what your data looks like and which methods suit it,
  before you model (exploratory data analysis guidance).
- **Built-in R Console** — optionally run arbitrary R on your data.
- **Plain-English results** and standard metrics (RMSE, R², accuracy, etc.) alongside tables
  and downloadable plots.

## Data it accepts

CSV, Excel (.xlsx), delimited text; and spatial formats: GeoTIFF (.tif) rasters, LAS/LAZ LiDAR
point clouds, GeoJSON, GeoPackage (.gpkg) and Shapefiles. Datasets can also be typed or pasted
in from scratch.

## Analyses available

- **Statistical models**: linear regression, ANOVA, linear mixed-effects models, logistic
  regression, discriminant analysis (LDA/QDA/LLDA/RLDA and more), principal component analysis
  (PCA), and statistical tests.
- **Machine learning**: random forest, support vector machines, neural networks, decision
  trees, gradient boosting (XGBoost), classification, and clustering (k-means, hierarchical,
  PAM/Gower).
- **Spatial & LiDAR / remote sensing**: point-cloud viewing, canopy height models and
  individual tree detection, raster analysis, terrain and surface analysis, hydrological
  analysis, and satellite data search/download.
- **Other**: time-series, survival analysis, structural equation modelling (SEM), Bayesian
  analysis, and generalized additive models (GAM).

## How it works (technical)

EasyAnalysis is an R Shiny application compiled to WebAssembly with Shinylive and served as a
static site (hosted on Vercel). All computation happens client-side in the browser via webR;
there is no analysis backend. The AI Co-Pilot calls the OpenAI API (the user may supply their
own key, or use the deployment's key via a serverless proxy) using tool-calling that runs the
app's own analysis functions.

## Privacy

Uploaded data is processed only in the user's browser and is never transmitted to a server.
The AI Co-Pilot sends only what the user asks about (plus the current screen's context) to the
language model, and only when the user sends a message.

## Notes

- First visit takes about 3–5 minutes while the R environment downloads into the browser; it
  loads instantly from cache afterwards.
- EasyAnalysis is an independent project. The University of Eastern Finland is acknowledged for
  code contributions and for data used in analyses and testing.
- Author: Tim Casanda Gibson.

## Links

- App: https://easyanalysis.vercel.app
- In-app Documentation and References screens describe usage and the published methods
  implemented.
